clue.text: Man with skill considered sincere

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
art is skill or craft
felt means considered or believed

explanation.surface: A capable man is judged to be genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heartfelt is deeply and genuinely meant, a synonym for sincere.

clue.text: Grave words

parts.note: grave reads as solemn, but it is the burial place, so these are words inscribed on a tomb

explanation.definitionFit: An inscription on a headstone is literally words on a grave.

clue.text: Contralto has it in sincere performance

indicators.note: in tells us the contralto and it sit inside the word for sincere

parts.note: real means sincere or genuine
C is a standard abbreviation for contralto in music

explanation.surface: A contralto puts heartfelt feeling into her singing.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a musical performance given by a soloist or small group.

clue.text: Ruby, or 2.5 percent of one?

definitions.meaning: a ruby wedding anniversary marks forty years of marriage
two and a half percent of a whole is one part in forty

explanation.surface: A jeweller weighs whether a ruby is worth a tiny fraction of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruby is the traditional gift for the anniversary numbered forty, and one part in forty is 2.5 percent.

clue.text: Some indignant ouches — you hit me!

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone yelps indignantly after being struck, conceding the blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Touché is the fencer's admission of being struck, used generally to concede a fair point.

clue.text: Author's fiction title

parts.note: not the name of a novel, but a made-up name the writer goes by

explanation.definitionFit: A pen name is a fictitious name under which a writer publishes.

clue.text: See pigeon die after eating insect

indicators.note: eating means the word for die swallows the insect

parts.note: to fail is to die or stop working, as an engine does
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A bird is watched dying after swallowing a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' and 'after' are only link words here.
explanation.definitionFit: The fantail is a breed of domestic pigeon with a fan-shaped tail.

clue.text: Mark of grief at an artiste's performance

indicators.note: performance suggests the letters of the words before it being worked into a new form

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: An audience weeps at a singer's moving show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performance' rearranges ANARTISTE; 'at' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain left by tears on the cheek or a letter is a sign of sorrow.

clue.text: Acting as agent, so busy

indicators.note: busy suggests the letters bustling about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone standing in as agent finds themselves very occupied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busy' rearranges AGENTSO; 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on stage means performing in a play, which is acting.

clue.text: Failing in suit, give away one's heart, perhaps

definitions.text: Failing in suit, give away one's heart, perhaps

parts.words: Failing in suit, give away one's heart, perhaps
parts.note: reads like romance, but in card play a player unable to follow the suit led throws away a card, such as a heart

explanation.definitionFit: In whist or bridge, to throw an unwanted card when unable to follow suit is the standard term.

clue.text: After class, complete confusion

indicators.note: After says the word for complete comes behind the abbreviation for class

parts.note: CL is an abbreviation for class
utter means complete or total

explanation.surface: After a lesson the room is in total chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Clutter is an untidy jumble, a state of disorder.

clue.text: To survive, abandon such desperate resistance?

parts.note: to last is to survive or endure
to ditch is to abandon

explanation.surface: A defender wonders whether to give up a hopeless stand in order to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such' and 'resistance?' frame the definition: a final effort is made in the last trench.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-ditch effort is a final desperate attempt to avert disaster.

clue.text: Man offering central heating to French city

parts.note: Arles is a city in Provence, southern France

explanation.surface: A man installs radiators for a town in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles is a man's first name.

clue.text: Pleasure-seeker — noted his downfall

indicators.note: downfall suggests the letters collapsing and being rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone notes that self-indulgence caused his ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedonist lives for pleasure, a devoted seeker of enjoyment.

clue.text: Make pounds in card game, though

indicators.note: in places the pounds symbol inside the card game

parts.note: whist is a trick-taking card game
L stands for pounds, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: Winning money at cards is the aim, nevertheless.
explanation.definitionFit: Whilst is a British variant of while, meaning although.

clue.text: Unkempt, having suffered a blow

definitions.meaning: untidy or dishevelled, especially of hair
battered by the wind, as though struck

explanation.surface: Someone looks dishevelled after being punched.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair tousled by gusts looks dishevelled, and a place exposed to gales has literally been blown on.

clue.text: Most regular meal fails to fill a good chap

indicators.note: to fill means the meal and the failing go inside the saint

parts.note: ST, saint, is crosswordese for a good man
tea is an afternoon or evening meal in Britain
dies means fails or stops working

explanation.surface: A good man's dinner falls through.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadiest means most even or constant, the most regular in pace.

clue.text: Those people accept charge for treatment

indicators.note: accept means the word for those people takes the charge in

parts.note: they refers to those people
a rap is a criminal charge, as in taking the rap

explanation.surface: A group admits being accused and is sent for treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is medical or psychological treatment.

clue.text: Blocked pedestrian's path

parts.note: seems to describe an obstructed walkway, but means a footway laid with paving blocks

explanation.definitionFit: A British footway beside a road is laid with paving slabs, the walker's route.

clue.text: Bird in no way fat

parts.note: O, zero, means nothing or no
ST, street, is a way
rich food is fatty

explanation.surface: A bird that is by no means plump.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is a large flightless African bird.

clue.text: Cause astonishment endlessly on river

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for causing astonishment loses its final letter

parts.note: to amaze is to cause astonishment

explanation.surface: Something keeps astounding people as it flows along a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazon is the great river of South America.

clue.text: A strain, working, for him?

indicators.note: working suggests the letters being worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A craftsman under strain at his labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges ASTRAIN; the whole clue also describes the skilled worker who toils.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman works with his hands, so strain at work suits him.

clue.text: Order in America includes nothing threatening

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

indicators.note: includes means the words for in America take nothing inside them

parts.note: US is America
O, the figure zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: A command in the United States contains nothing alarming.
explanation.definitionFit: Ominous means menacing, giving a sense of danger ahead.

clue.text: Sit out in ball, showing aloofness

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the word for ball

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A wallflower sits out at a ball, appearing standoffish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SIT into IST, which 'in' puts inside DANCE; 'showing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping one's distance means emotional reserve, coolness towards others.

clue.text: All the actors, or a single star

parts.note: the cast is all the actors in a production

explanation.surface: A whole company of actors, or just one leading performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star' looks theatrical but means a heavenly body: Castor is one of the twin stars of Gemini.
explanation.definitionFit: Castor is a bright star in the constellation Gemini.

clue.text: Find out for sure

parts.note: a plain description of establishing a fact with certainty, with the last two words hinting at a sense of being certain

explanation.definitionFit: To establish a fact definitely by checking is the dictionary sense.

clue.text: Bishop, one surrounded by troubles and concerns

indicators.note: surrounded by means the bishop and one sit inside the word for troubles

parts.note: woes are troubles
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A bishop is beset by difficulties and anxieties.
explanation.definitionFit: Worries are anxieties, matters that concern a person.

clue.text: The soap is slippery in this place to eat

indicators.note: slippery suggests the letters sliding about into a new order

explanation.surface: The soap in a cafe washroom keeps slipping out of hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is slippery' rearranges THESOAP; 'in this' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearoom serving light meals is somewhere to eat.

clue.text: Fool round after film, "the Spanish artist"

indicators.note: after says the fool and the round come behind the word for film

parts.note: a pic is a film, short for picture
an ass is a fool
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone clowns about after a movie about a famous painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso was the celebrated Spanish painter and co-founder of Cubism.

clue.text: Lack of practice in oxidising process?

definitions.meaning: being out of practice at a skill
the corrosion of iron when it oxidises

explanation.surface: Neglect of training likened to metal corroding.
explanation.definitionFit: Skills unused grow stiff like corroded iron, and iron left exposed oxidises into a reddish coating.
